assign.request: Run the auditor on why padding decisions keep going wrong. What do layout, css and the ui skills say about padding? Are containers declared as container-type so the units work in sidebars, columns and nested cases? Should --pad move to container units; is one token right or two? Plus: name the container-query failure modes this site has actually hit; measure whether the cq tokens cost paint time during a resize; and weigh the owner's own proposal - a `card` class that carries the default pad, so a card is by definition padded.
assign.now: measuring what --pad actually computes to in five hosts at four widths
steps: Read the token block, the .pad rule and the rungs in framework.css
Measure used padding and the resolved tokens in five hosts at four widths
Census container-type; name the cq failure modes from the record
A/B the resize cost with the token block neutralised
The judgment: one token or two, percent or container units, and the card word
Rank the changes; apply the fail-safe edits; write the rest as decisions

log.msg: MEASURED (headless, four widths, used padding read geometrically): a .pad box gets 14 / 16.7 / 32.3 / 69.6 px in a full-width PAGE REGION, and 14 / 15 / 16 / 18 px in a nested card, 12 / 12.8 / 14.4 in the site sidebar, 12.8 everywhere in the dev bar. Reason: --pad is calc(clamp(1em, 2.6% - 1.1em, 4em) * --size), and 2.6% of the containing block only passes the 1em floor once that block is about 1292px wide. So --pad is FLAT AT ITS FLOOR for every card, rail and column on the site, and ramps only on full-width regions - a 4.3x spread at 3440 between two boxes wearing the same word.

MEASURED: a percentage inside calc() STAYS a percentage in the computed value, so getComputedStyle(el).paddingLeft reads back as a calc() string, not px - parseFloat gives NaN. Padding on this site cannot be verified numerically the obvious way; it has to be measured geometrically (an inner span left edge minus the box left edge). That alone explains a lot of unverified padding work.

MEASURED: neither core/Sidebar nor dev/DevBar declares container-type (grep: zero hits in either dir), so the cqi terms in --gap and --flow resolve against the VIEWPORT inside them. The sidebar --gap is 15.6 / 25 / 34.6 px at 1280 / 1920 / 3440 inside a 240-287px rail; the dev bar --gap is 30.7px at 3440 inside a 271px bar. Containers that ARE declared: .stage, .page-preview-thumb, .demo-stage, .v3, the AITask card, the homepage default region, ux/Wizard, several labs. Page.css lines 318, 846, 888, 939 record the deliberate decision NOT to make .page or a rail a container: container-type applies layout containment and makes the box a containing block for position: fixed.

MEASURED (performance A/B, 3s of continuous viewport resizing, CDP Performance metrics): /framework/core/Page/ tokens live - style 1.734s / 8018 recalcs, layout 0.676s / 668 layouts, 181 frames, ZERO long frames over 50ms; the same page with the cq token block neutralised to plain em - style 1.478s, layout 0.827s, 181 frames, zero long frames. /layouts/shell/ live 1.437s style / 0.868s layout vs neutralised 1.301s / 0.947s. Seven ResizeObservers and one window resize listener on the Page demo, five and one on shell. VERDICT: the tokens are not the cost - neutralising them moves nothing outside noise and produces no long frames at 60fps. If the fans spin while resizing, the file watcher, LiveReload and the supervisor are the better suspects (the fans skill).

decision.about: CHANGE 1 - the owner's own proposal: a card class that carries the default pad, so a card is by definition padded

options.say: framework.css gains six lines: .card { background: var(--surface); color: var(--ink); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: var(--radius); padding: var(--pad-card); } - and .card.size-small for dense UIs (the dev bar), reusing the --size knob that already exists rather than inventing a .tight word
leave it as today: write .surface and remember to add .pad

decision.because: MEASURED: framework.css has NO card word at all. .surface carries ground, ink, a hairline and a radius and NO padding, so every padded box is two words the writer has to remember - and 180 distinct hand-rolled card/tile class names exist across the site's CSS. Every one of today's failures is that missing word: the V3 tiles are a .surface with no .pad; the dev bar cards were a hand-written 0.4em 0.5em (devbar-chat measured 5.12px, and proved --pad itself was fine at 12.8px); the mastermind wrote two private ramps because there was nothing to reach for. The name is the owner's own and passes their naming rule - a word that describes many boxes, and this is the one that helps.
decision.alternative_cost: one more word in the vocabulary, and a card word invites .card.wide/.card.tight sprawl - which is why the dense variant reuses the existing --size knob instead of a new word
decision.owner: framework.css is the owner's to approve; a task can land it in one write

decision.about: CHANGE 2 - should --pad move from a percentage to container units, as the owner keeps suggesting, and is one token right or two?

options.say: keep the percentage for --pad (regions, unchanged) and give the new card word its own band in the owner's numbers: --pad-card: clamp(0.5em, 2.6%, 2em). Two tokens, one rule an agent can apply without thinking: a REGION takes .pad, a FRAMED BOX takes .card, a CONTROL or row stays in its own em.
one token for everything at the owner's band, clamp(0.5em, 2.6%, 2em) - regions then cap at 2em (36px at 3440) instead of today's 69.6px

decision.because: MEASURED, and it inverts the intuition: a PADDING percentage resolves against the containing block's width, which for a box that fills its slot is the same thing cqi would give - and it needs NO container-type anywhere. cqi does need one, and this site deliberately refuses container-type on .page and on rails (Page.css 318/846/888/939: layout containment, and the box becomes a containing block for position: fixed). Inside the sidebar and the dev bar - neither of which is a container - cqi reads the VIEWPORT: --gap there is already 34.6px and 30.7px at 3440 inside a 287px and a 271px box. Moving --pad to cqi today would make those rails WORSE, not better. The real defect is the numbers, not the unit: 2.6% - 1.1em only clears the 1em floor once the containing block is about 1292px wide, so --pad is pinned flat at 1em for every card, rail and column (measured 14/15/16/18px) while a full-width region ramps to 69.6px - the same word, a 4.3x spread, nothing in the CSS to show it. Two tokens because the region ramp is doing real work at 3440 and the owner's 0.5em-2em band is a CARD band; one token would have to pick one ceiling for both.
decision.alternative_cost: two tokens is one more thing to know - paid for by the fact that the rule fits on one line and the class names say which is which

decision.about: CHANGE 3 - the sidebar and the dev bar use cqi tokens but are not query containers, so those tokens read the viewport

options.say: declare container-type: inline-size on the sidebar's inner rail and the dev bar's body, and re-measure the four failure modes (shrink-to-fit collapse, fixed-position children, self-query, nested em) on both
leave both boxes alone and have their own CSS declare gap/flow in the rail's own em, which is what a fixed-width rail actually wants

decision.because: a rail DECLARES its width - it is not a box that adapts to its slot - so the honest unit inside it is its own em, exactly what Page.css already concluded for side regions (line 888: a side box declares its width, so the honest answer is a fraction of THAT, no extra element and no container-type). Declaring container-type on a rail is the change this codebase has been bitten by most: a flex column with containment measured 0px while holding 963px of children, a Stage shrank to 307px inside a 1546px frame, and the blog hero set one character per line. The measured symptom (34.6px between rows in a 287px rail at 3440) is fixed either way; this way costs two lines of CSS and no containment risk.
decision.alternative_cost: the rails then do not respond to their own width if they ever become resizable-to-anything - acceptable: both have a fixed range, and a container can be declared later on the inner wrapper if a real need appears

decision.about: CHANGE 4 - the mechanical half, since three of four failing agents this week never loaded the css or layout skill at all

options.say: two rules in the page-health watcher being built today (ai/2026-09-19/page-health/): (1) an element with a border AND a background AND used padding under 8px is a finding - it is a card someone forgot to pad; (2) a row inside a list taller than 40px is a finding - it is page-scale spacing on control-scale rows. Both measured geometrically, because a % inside calc() reads back from getComputedStyle as a calc string, never px.
write the padding rule more prominently in css and layout

decision.because: this morning's audit measured that three of the four agents that shipped bad spacing never loaded css or layout - better words would not have been read. Both of today's padding complaints are one number each and a machine can see them: the dev bar cards were 5.12px with a border and a ground, and the sidebar rows were 46.5px in a list. assign.outcome:
**The token is not broken; the vocabulary is missing a word.** [/framework/ai/2026-09-19/padding-audit/](/framework/ai/2026-09-19/padding-audit/)

**Measured, four widths, used padding read geometrically.** `--pad` is a percentage of the containing block, so it stays pinned at its 1em floor until that block is ~1292px wide: a `.pad` box is **14 / 15 / 16 / 18px** in a card, a rail or a column and **14 / 16.7 / 32.3 / 69.6px** in a full-width region — the same word, a 4.3× spread. And framework.css has **no `card` word at all**: `.surface` is ground + hairline + radius with no padding, so a padded box is two words you must remember — and **180 hand-rolled card/tile classes** across the site are what happened instead.

**The owner's proposal is the right one, and it is the top change:** `.card` = ground + hairline + radius + the default pad, `.card.size-small` for dense UIs (reusing the existing `--size` knob, not a new word). It would have prevented the V3 tiles with no top padding, the dev bar's hand-written `0.4em 0.5em` (5.12px) and both hand-written ramps.

**On container units — the measurement inverts the intuition.** Keep the percentage. A padding `%` resolves against the box that holds you, which for a box filling its slot is what `cqi` would give, and it needs no `container-type` anywhere. Neither the sidebar nor the dev bar is a container, so `cqi` there reads the **viewport**: `--gap` is already **34.6px in a 287px rail** and **30.7px in a 271px bar** at 3440. Moving `--pad` to `cqi` today makes the rails worse. The defect is the numbers: the owner's band (0.5em–2em) is a CARD band — hence two tokens, one rule: **region → `.pad`, framed box → `.card`, control or row → its own `em`.**

**Container queries have bitten this site five ways** (self-query; containment collapsing a content-sized box — 0px holding 963px, a Stage at 307px, the blog hero at one character per line; viewport fallback; `em` resolving against the container; and `container-type` making the box a containing block for `position: fixed`). That is why `.page` and the rails are deliberately not containers.

**Performance: the tokens are not the cost.** Three seconds of continuous resizing — 181 frames, **zero frames over 50ms**; style 1.73s / layout 0.68s with the tokens live versus 1.48s / 0.83s neutralised to plain `em` (noise, and layout got *slower* without them). Seven ResizeObservers, one resize listener. If the fans spin while resizing, the watcher, LiveReload and the supervisor are the suspects.

**Applied (fail-safe):** the layout skill said multipliers are no longer allowed and then used one two bullets later — it now points at the rung; two css caveats — `--pad` is floor-pinned under a ~1292px block, and a `%` inside `calc()` reads back from `getComputedStyle` as a string, so padding can only be measured geometrically (which is why so much padding work went unverified).

**Waiting on the owner** (four `decision` lines, each with its alternative): the `card` word · percentage + two tokens rather than container units + one · the rails' own `em` instead of `cqi` · two lint rules for the page-health watcher (a bordered box with under 8px of padding; a list row over 40px). `framework.css` was not edited.
